claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one, for all 1 <= j_1 <= j_2 <= l_1 (the Leighton-Shor scale), every partition of [0,1]^2 into dyadic squares of sides between 2^(-j_2) and 2^(-j_1), every H constant on its cells and every c: |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N ((j_1^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V^c(H) + (j_2^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V^c_f(H)), V^c the cell variation (jumps times edge lengths, boundary edges against c) and V^c_f its part over fine edges (partition edges that are not whole edges of the mesh 2^(-j_1)). For a closed simple curve on the partition's edges, the bound is L sqrt N ((j_1^(3/4)+sqrt(log N)) l(C) + (j_2^(3/4)+sqrt(log N)) l_f(C)).
claims.assessment: Working proof: each run of fine edges of a curve ends at coarse vertices and is closed by a coarse staircase no longer than it; the curve splits as a chain into a coarse closed chain of mass at most its length and fine closed chains of mass at most twice the fine length; closed integer chains split into simple closed curves with additive winding numbers; lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (a) at both meshes; layer cake.
claims.rationale: Lets a cell function pay the fine mesh's Leighton-Shor factor only on its fine edges, a step toward adapting the mesh to the gradient level in the coarea mechanism for conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy.
claims.next_action: Iterate the staircase step over a graded partition with geometrically spaced meshes, and bound the interface sum and the coarse level's mass near the fine support.
